sections.heading: Impact
paragraphs: Per the file, dapp developers: Enables non-disruptive rent increases. Per the file, existing accts are grandfathered at their (per the file) creation-time rent price until (per the file) they increase in size. Per the file, new accts and accts that have increased in (per the file) size adopt the current rent price. Per the file, minimal behavior change for (per the file) typical applications; most applications fail to reduce acct balances below their minimum during normal operation. Per the file, validators: Minimal performance impact; calls for storing pre-execution balance (one (per the file) u64) and size per write-locked acct during tx execution. Per the file, core contributors: Changes to tx processing logic to capture (per the file) pre-execution state and implement (per the file) the relaxed balance check. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Security Considerations
paragraphs: Per the file, enables safe rent increases without disrupting existing accts: only newly allocated accts are subject to new rent prices. Per the file, maintains the invariant that accts always satisfy the minimum (per the file) rent price since the (per the file) time of their most recent allocation. Per the file, no mechanism for forcing accts to "upgrade" to current (per the file) rent prices without upwards (per the file) reallocation; this is intentional (per the file) to preserve non-disruptiveness. Per the file, it's essentially free to (per the file) adopt a new rent rate (per the file) that's lower than the rent (per the file) rate an acct was subject to at allocation time.

Per the file, this isn't problematic in (per the file) itself but it may cause (per the file) users to be less sensitive (per the file) to rent increases. Per the file, for similar reasons, there's (per the file) potential for a secondary state (per the file) market to develop, leading to (per the file) an additional sudden increase in (per the file) state allocation in anticipation of (per the file) a future rent hike. Per the file, this can further exacerbate (per the file) an excessive state growth event. Per the file, the owner change check (per the file) during minimum balance calculation (per the file) is intended to limit (per the file) this by making reselling accts more difficult. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

Per the file, this is backwards compatible (per the file) in the sense that txs that currently succeed will continue to succeed.
